photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: A reproduced newspaper photo of Piegan Blackfeet Chief Big Spring and his wife in traditional dress (feather headdress, decorated hide shirt and leggings, beaded dress), clearly identified by the caption and matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The photograph shows Plains Native men and women in feathered war bonnets, beaded and fringed regalia, mounted on horses with full tack, beside tipis — a documentary image of Plains Indian dress and encampment life entirely consistent with (though not provably specific to) Piegan Blackfeet material culture; regalia of this type cannot be distinguished from neighboring Plains groups, which is acceptable.

photo.name: photographic print; glass negative
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: The photo documents a named South Piegan (Blackfeet) chief, Big Spring, and his wife in full traditional dress (feather headdress, decorated hide shirt, leggings, and beaded cloth dress) outdoors in Montana — a clear documentary photo of the claimed people's attire and life.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white and halftone lithographic colour); photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Piegan man, Acustie (Many Diving), wearing a horned ermine-trimmed headdress, decorated tunic, leggings, fur and shell choker, and beaded bracelets — documentary dress photo matching the claimed Piegan Blackfeet identity.
